transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam Patel (Redwood SE); Tom Keller (Procurement - NebulaHealth); Aisha Rahman (Head of Security - NebulaHealth); Dr. Priya Sharma (CTO - NebulaHealth); Jorge Morales (Legal Counsel - NebulaHealth)

Summary: High level procurement intake and legal redline walkthrough, included initial pricing discussion, SLA clarity, and technical pre-checks for a Dedicated/private deployment.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, we got Tom, Aisha, Priya, Jorge?
[00:08] Tom Keller: Yep, that's us. Thanks Maya. Appreciate you fitting this in.
[00:12] Maya Chen: For context, Liam from our SE team will cover the technical constraints, I'll handle commercial / legal flow. Aim is to come out with a clear list of redlines and next steps.
[00:22] Liam Patel: hi all. quick note: we looked at Nebula's attachment re: throughput and the 90th percentile latency targets and we'll propose two pricing paths, reserved capacity and dedicated pool, plus a private deployment option.
[00:35] Aisha Rahman: Sorry to inter— quick Q up front; our security bar: SOC 2 type II and KMS with customer-managed keys, we need audit logs kept for three years. Is that supported?
[00:47] Maya Chen: short answer yes to both; we have SOC 2 and can integrate with your KMS/HSM. retention windows are configurable; we'll include that in the security packet.
[00:55] Jorge Morales: on the DPA, we have standard NHS-like clauses — data residency in eu-west-1 for all patient PII, plus no subprocessing without notice. We will likely redline subprocessor clause.
[01:08] Maya Chen: understood. we have region pinning for Private and Dedicated; hosted can be restricted but we'll call out the routing. also, we can add an explicit subprocessor notification SLA in the DPA.
[01:20] Tom Keller: pricing— can you walk through the delta between reserved capacity and hosted? Our finance team is particularly sensitive to committed spend.
[01:30] Liam Patel: sure. reserved gives you predictable throughput at lower unit cost if you commit; hosted is pay-as-you-go but unit cost is higher. we also offer a burst policy on reserved for spikes. for example, at your projected 25M tokens/month, reserved reduces per-token cost by roughly 30–40% versus hosted. that delta scales with commit.
[01:48] Dr. Priya Sharma: what's included in the SLA? uptime, latency SLOs, and support RTO? we're concerned about 24x7 support for incident response.
[02:00] Maya Chen: standard SLA is 99.9% for hosted and 99.95% for Dedicated with enhanced support tiers. we can add a dedicated on-call and response time in the enterprise package; typical RTO for Sev1 is one hour with a committed war room.
[02:14] Aisha Rahman: Latency SLO for inference is tricky— our product needs P95 under 250ms on average. can you commit that across multi-tenant hosted?
[02:24] Liam Patel: P95 250ms is tight on hosted at peak; dedicated gives better headroom. also quantization and batching profiles affect tail latency. we'll run a perf bench using your sample traffic to validate.
[02:36] Tom Keller: what about egress and network fees? our cloud team is sensitive.
[02:40] Maya Chen: egress fees depend on deployment; Private deployments typically avoid cloud egress fees if peered into your VPC. Hosted would follow normal cloud egress. we'll include a cost estimate in the pricing matrix.
[02:54] Jorge Morales: on indemnities — we will likely request stronger IP indemnity and limitation of liability caps aligned to contract value. can Redwood do that?
[03:05] Maya Chen: standard we have is mutual indemnity with defined caps; for enterprise deals we can negotiate liability caps tied to committed spend. we'll flag this for legal.
[03:17] Dr. Priya Sharma: timeline— procurement wants a decision by end of Q2. is that doable?
[03:22] Tom Keller: yes, end of Q2 ideally. we need price certainty and MSA/DPA agreed earlier.
[03:28] Liam Patel: operationally we can kick off a pilot in two weeks once we have the NDA in place and sample traffic. full rollout depends on legal window.
[03:36] Maya Chen: ok let's align on immediate deliverables. we'll send annotated MSA/DPA with suggested redlines, security packet with SOC 2 docs, and a pricing matrix with reserved vs hosted vs private economics.
[03:48] Aisha Rahman: please call out KMS flow: who holds the keys, rotation policies, and whether we can use BYOK with HSM.
[03:56] Liam Patel: BYOK is supported in Private and Dedicated modes; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via supported KMS integrations but there are nuances— we'll document exact flows.
[04:08] Jorge Morales: can you confirm audit log retention and accessibility for compliance audits? we may require a signed attestation.
[04:15] Maya Chen: yes. we'll include log retention settings and can provide an attestation letter as part of the security packet.
[04:24] Tom Keller: procurement will also want a path for termination and data egress — how quickly can we get data back in the clear?
[04:31] Liam Patel: standard is 30 days export access after termination; we can discuss expedited egress options for an additional fee. for Private deployments you'll control the data store so that's flexible.
[04:44] Dr. Priya Sharma: ok, on the technical side, we'll need a runbook for spike handling and a breakdown of throttling behavior.
[04:52] Liam Patel: yes, we'll share our autoscale + throttling doc and the recommended batch sizes for your model shapes.
[05:00] Maya Chen: any blockers from legal on our side?
[05:03] Jorge Morales: few: subprocessor notification, liability cap, termination for convenience fee, and a clearer data residency clause. we'll send redlines.
[05:12] Maya Chen: fair. on pricing, we can present two commercial options: a 12‑month reserved commit with discounted unit price, or a 3‑month pilot at market rates then commit. which would you prefer?
[05:25] Tom Keller: Finance likes the predictable cost but legal may push back on long lock-ins. maybe pilot then commit is safer.
[05:31] Dr. Priya Sharma: pilot-first looks better; we can validate latency and error rates before committing.
[05:36] Maya Chen: ok we will propose a 90‑day pilot with a reserved pilot cluster and a conversion credit if you commit to 12 months.
[05:46] Aisha Rahman: small note — our compliance team requires proof of subprocessor mapping and a list of physical locations where logs are stored.
[05:55] Liam Patel: we'll include an inventory of subprocessors and a map of storage regions in the security packet.
[06:02] Maya Chen: recap and next steps: one, I (Maya) will send annotated MSA/DPA and pricing matrix by 2026‑03‑18. two, Liam will run a perf bench using your sample traffic and share results by 2026‑03‑21. three, Jorge will consolidate legal redlines by 2026‑03‑20. four, Tom to provide monthly token volumes and P95 targets by 2026‑03‑16. five, schedule a technical deep dive w/ infra week of 2026‑03‑23.
[06:30] Tom Keller: that sounds good. any open questions?
[06:33] Jorge Morales: one more — on escrow/escrow-like custody for model weights if we go Private, what's the path?
[06:41] Liam Patel: we have options — bring-your-own weights inside your VPC, or we can arrange an escrow arrangement for model artifacts. we'll follow up with a short note.
[06:51] Dr. Priya Sharma: ok thanks everyone. we'll review the packet when it arrives and circle back with marked redlines.
[06:58] Maya Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
[07:05] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional overlap and misattributions; native transcription had a few misheard words (e.g., redwood -> redwook) that were corrected manually where obvious.
